Description: OntoKSD competency framework (subset) focused on automata and formal models. Default scale: Beginner, Intermediate, Advanced, Expert.

Short name: Competence: Justify the use of Deterministic Finite Automata (DFAs)
Description: This competency focuses on students' ability to distinguish between deterministic and non-deterministic finite automata, and evaluate which model is best suited to a given problem.
Review deterministic finite automata and demonstrate comprehension at the 'Understanding' level of Bloom's taxonomy.

Short name: KS-Pair: Apply requirements specification using automata
Description: Apply requirements specification techniques to automata, aligning with the 'Applying' level of Bloom's taxonomy.

Short name: KS-Pair: Apply analytical thinking to automata problems
Description: Use analytical reasoning when evaluating which model is most suited for a problem, aligning with Bloom's 'Applying'.
Adopt an investigative approach to analyzing automata models.
Collaborate with peers to justify model selection and discuss trade-offs.
Show responsibility in evaluating implications of choosing one automata model over another.
Take initiative in identifying scenarios where DFAs are the most appropriate model.

This competency relates to the use of simulation tools (e.g., JFLAP) to verify the correctness and behavior of automata implementations. It emphasizes systematic testing and iterative refinement of state-machine models.
Apply finite state machine concepts when designing and testing automata.

Short name: KS-Pair: Apply problem solving and troubleshooting
Description: Use problem-solving and troubleshooting strategies to identify and correct issues in automata implementations.

Short name: KS-Pair: Apply foundational approaches to validating models
Description: Apply formal validation methods to assess automata correctness and robustness.
Investigate systematically the correctness and behavior of automata using simulators.
Collaborate in teams to validate automata implementations.
Act responsibly in interpreting test outcomes and suggesting refinements.
Proactively design diverse test cases to explore edge conditions in automata models.
Use creativity in devising test scenarios and exploring unexpected behaviors in state machines.
